topic.title: Synaptic Computation and Spike-Based Learning
topic.overview: Synapses and spike timing can contribute computation beyond the static weighted sums used in many neural networks. This topic studies stochastic transmission, dynamic synaptic efficacy, Hebbian plasticity, and efficient spike-based representations. It connects biological hypotheses about learning with trainable models that must handle discrete events and temporal dependence.
topic.whyItMatters: Treating synapses as dynamic units can reveal how recent activity changes information processing. Translating such mechanisms into artificial systems raises a separate optimization problem because hard spikes are not ordinarily differentiable. Biological plausibility, computational efficiency, and task accuracy therefore require distinct evaluation.
topic.evolution: A 1987 physiological analysis relates synaptic potentials to firing correlations. A 1997 model shows how dynamic stochastic synapses can increase computational capabilities, followed by work on spike-timing plasticity and efficient coding. UltraLIF in 2026 uses ultradiscretization and smooth max-plus relaxations to train spiking dynamics with standard backpropagation under its mathematical formulation.
openQuestions: Which synaptic dynamics contribute capabilities unavailable to static-weight approximations?
How closely can differentiable spike models preserve event timing while remaining easy to optimize?

papers.title: Learning optimal spike-based representations
papers.tldr: Optimizing a fixed linear readout yields a spiking network whose learning produces sparse firing, balanced activity, and predictive coding.

papers.title: Neuronal Spike Generation Mechanism as an Oversampling, Noise-shaping A-to-D converter
papers.tldr: Data from three neuron classes support a noise-shaping account of spike generation as analog-to-digital conversion.

papers.title: Spiking and saturating dendrites differentially expand single neuron computation capacity
papers.tldr: Both dendritic behaviors expand a binary neuron's computational capacity, but spiking can require exponentially fewer units for an important family of functions.

papers.title: Towards a learning-theoretic analysis of spike-timing dependent plasticity
papers.tldr: An analyzable neuron model links spike quality to synaptic strength and motivates a more robust, regularized plasticity rule.

papers.title: Waveform Driven Plasticity in BiFeO3 Memristive Devices: Model and Implementation
papers.tldr: A biologically motivated waveform model enables timing-dependent and triplet plasticity in BiFeO3 memristive devices.

papers.title: A memory frontier for complex synapses
papers.tldr: The paper develops theorems linking the internal organization of complex synapses to their memory properties.

papers.title: Firing rate predictions in optimal balanced networks
papers.tldr: Treating optimal balanced network dynamics as an optimization algorithm yields firing-rate predictions linked directly to input, connectivity, and computational function.

papers.title: Perfect Associative Learning with Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity
papers.tldr: Specific excitatory and inhibitory timing-dependent plasticity mechanisms, combined with neuronal hyperpolarization, suffice to implement perceptron learning.

papers.title: A framework for studying synaptic plasticity with neural spike train data
papers.tldr: A Bayesian framework jointly infers changing neural connections and plasticity rules, recovering both from simulated spike trains.

papers.title: A Synaptical Story of Persistent Activity with Graded Lifetime in a Neural System
papers.tldr: Combining short-term synaptic facilitation and depression can produce persistent neural activity with variable lifetimes that ends naturally.

papers.title: Inferring synaptic conductances from spike trains with a biophysically inspired point process model
papers.tldr: A conductance-based spike model extends the GLM and accurately infers excitatory and inhibitory conductances from extracellular recordings in the tested retinal cells.

papers.title: Real-Time Decoding of an Integrate and Fire Encoder
papers.tldr: A causal integrate-and-fire decoder reconstructs signals in real time with error bounds tied to elapsed time, spike density, and signal properties.

papers.title: Synaptic Sampling: A Bayesian Approach to Neural Network Plasticity and Rewiring
papers.tldr: Synaptic sampling models plasticity as Bayesian posterior sampling and shows continuous compensation for unexpected disturbances in spiking-network simulations.

papers.title: Efficient Neural Codes under Metabolic Constraints
papers.tldr: A theory of neural coding under noise and energy constraints predicts budget-dependent responses and increasing efficiency advantages for ON–OFF pairs.

papers.title: Objective and efficient inference for couplings in neuronal networks
papers.tldr: An analytic screening approximation makes neuronal coupling inference cheaper while supporting accurate reconstruction from simulated and cultured-network spike data.

papers.title: Nonlinear scaling of resource allocation in sensory bottlenecks
papers.tldr: Efficient coding models predict that sensory-region magnification depends nonlinearly on both receptor density and the total output capacity available.

papers.title: Lamina-specific neuronal properties promote robust, stable signal propagation in feedforward networks
papers.tldr: Differences in neuronal properties across layers can counteract preceding signal distortions and improve information transmission through feedforward networks.

papers.title: Minimax Dynamics of Optimally Balanced Spiking Networks of Excitatory and Inhibitory Neurons
papers.tldr: Deriving spiking networks from minimax objectives explains tight excitation-inhibition balance and predicts firing rates for specified computations.

papers.title: System Identification with Biophysical Constraints: A Circuit Model of the Inner Retina
papers.tldr: A biologically constrained retinal model predicts new responses and reproduces intervention effects while learning connectivity consistent with anatomical data.

papers.title: Using noise to probe recurrent neural network structure and prune synapses
papers.tldr: A local pruning rule uses noise-driven neural covariance and provably preserves dynamics under extensive pruning for a specified subset of networks.

papers.title: Online Learning Of Neural Computations From Sparse Temporal Feedback
papers.tldr: Sparse target-spike feedback can train both synaptic weights and intrinsic neuron parameters online without backpropagation through time.

papers.title: Biologically plausible solutions for spiking networks with efficient coding
papers.tldr: The paper builds efficient-coding spiking networks with richer biological features and connects excitatory connectivity rank to network responses.

papers.title: Emergence of Hierarchical Layers in a Single Sheet of Self-Organizing Spiking Neurons
papers.tldr: Local learning and dynamic connectivity let hierarchical layers and topographic maps emerge experimentally from an unstructured sheet of spiking neurons.

papers.title: The computational and learning benefits of Daleian neural networks
papers.tldr: The studied Daleian networks closely reproduce unrestricted computations, show greater resistance to synaptic noise, and learn effectively through neuron-level adjustments.

papers.title: Theoretically Provable Spiking Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Spiking networks with self-connections can approximate discrete dynamical systems with polynomial parameter counts and time complexity.

papers.title: Adaptive whitening with fast gain modulation and slow synaptic plasticity
papers.tldr: A sensory adaptation model combines slow synaptic learning with fast gain changes to whiten responses across changing statistical contexts.

papers.title: Dis-inhibitory neuronal circuits can control the sign of synaptic plasticity
papers.tldr: A proposed inhibitory microcircuit makes error-modulated Hebbian learning emerge under an explicit assumption about how top-down inputs encode errors.

papers.title: Neural Circuits for Fast Poisson Compressed Sensing in the Olfactory Bulb
papers.tldr: A biologically motivated circuit model decodes sparse odor mixtures within a sniff when its neural code matches receptor properties.

papers.title: Dendritic Resonate-and-Fire Neuron for Effective and Efficient Long Sequence Modeling
papers.tldr: A multi-branch spiking neuron combines frequency-specific processing with an adaptive firing threshold to model long sequences with sparse activity and competitive accuracy.

papers.title: Neural Correlates of Serial Dependence: Synaptic Short-term Plasticity Orchestrates Repulsion and Attraction
papers.tldr: A two-layer neural model explains perceptual repulsion and attraction through synaptic depression and facilitation operating at different processing stages.

papers.title: Seemingly Redundant Modules Enhance Robust Odor Learning in Fruit Flies
papers.tldr: A fly olfactory-circuit model shows that two seemingly redundant mechanisms complement each other across different noise conditions.

papers.title: Spike-timing-dependent Hebbian learning as noisy gradient descent
papers.tldr: A particular spike-timing-dependent Hebbian rule provably identifies the most active input neuron exponentially fast despite persistent noise.

papers.title: UltraLIF: Fully Differentiable Spiking Neural Networks via Ultradiscretization and Max-Plus Algebra
papers.tldr: UltraLIF derives differentiable spiking dynamics that approach hard thresholds, improving reported accuracy and enabling energy reductions through optional sparsity.
